You are a financial-analysis assistant.

Scenario description (context for your analysis):
Regulatory balancing accounts accumulate differences between revenues recognized and authorized revenue requirements until they are collected from customers or are refunded.  Regulatory balancing accounts include low-income programs and purchased-power and water accounts.  Debt-expense is amortized over the lives of the respective issues.  Call premiums on the redemption of long-term debt, as well as unamortized debt expense, are deferred and amortized to the extent they will be recovered through future service rates.  As a result of American Water Capital Corp.’s prepayment of certain senior notes and payment of a make-whole premium to the holders, the company recorded a charge resulting from the early extinguishment of debt at the parent company.  Substantially all of the early debt-extinguishment costs allocable to the company’s utility subsidiaries were recorded as regulatory assets that the company believes are probable of recovery in future rates.  Purchase-premium recoverable through rates is primarily the recovery of acquisition premiums related to earlier utility acquisitions.  These costs are being amortized through November 2048.  Tank-painting costs are generally deferred and amortized on a straight-line basis over periods ranging from two to fifteen years, as authorized by regulatory authorities.  Other regulatory assets include certain construction costs for treatment facilities, property-tax stabilization, employee-related costs, deferred other-post-retirement benefit expense, business-services project expenses, coastal-water project costs, rate-case expenditures and environmental-remediation costs, among others.  These costs are deferred because the amounts are being recovered in rates or are probable of recovery through rates in future periods.  Regulatory liabilities generally represent amounts that are probable of being credited or refunded to customers through the rate-making process.  Also, if costs expected to be incurred in the future are currently being recovered through rates, the company records those expected future costs as regulatory liabilities.  The company separately discloses regulatory-liability balances such as income-taxes recovered through rates, removal costs, pension and other post-retirement benefit balancing accounts, and other categories.
